body.statement: Fix \(\alpha\in[\delta_{\mathrm{ord}},1)\) when this range is nonempty. Do the exact finite coverage inequalities from \(\texttt{lem:deterministic-coverage-iff}\), together with lattice-consonance constraints, admit a deterministic exact procedure \(\widehat{\mathfrak O}^{\mathrm{cl}}_{\alpha}\) that has the same uniform simultaneous coverage as \(\widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}\), is contained in it for every observed table, is strictly contained for at least one nondegenerate compatible table, and remains computable solely through finitely many compatible response-table maximizations? Randomized reporting rules are outside this question.
body.justification: Below \(\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\) the frontier theorem rules out a deterministic strict contained refinement; at or above that threshold, a logically coherent exact refinement is the central open power problem.
body.gap: Mogstad et al. use stepwise directional testing, but no checked result supplies consonant closure for composite exact-quota schedule fibers with fixed arm totals.
body.consumer: A successful refinement would shorten simultaneous policy-rank reports without weakening the exact design guarantee used by small-cluster saturation trials.
